source_files.content:
# Advisory configuration variants (docs/testing.md#configuration-variants): make variants, the corpus
# JIT and AOT in configurations that CI's verification does not test and that must change no result:
# the IR passes off in the rows of a covering array of their pairs (PYSTACHY_OPT), and the runtime and
# AOT programs built at -O0 (PYSTACHY_CFLAGS). Each variant runs in four corpus shards.
# The lighter opt-1 and cflags-O0 rows share a build per shard. PRs use two workers with sampled cases.
# The full matrix runs daily, on demand and on relevant pushes to main. One same-run producer
# verifies the default compiler; every variant still builds its own private runtime cache.
name: Variants

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '23 6 * * *'   # daily, 06:23 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - .github/workflows/variants.yml
      - src/pystachy_compiler/specs.py
      - tests/corpus.sh
      - tests/run.sh
      - tools/shard_cases.sh
      - tools/verification_bootstrap.py
      - tools/merge_verification.py
      - tests/verify.sh
      - tools/variants.sh
concurrency:
  group: variants-${{ github.event.pull_request.number && format('pr-{0}', github.event.pull_request.number) || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  bootstrap:
    name: verified compiler producer
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      PYSTACHY_LLVM: /usr/lib/llvm-18/bin
      PYSTACHY_JOBS: '4'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0  # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version-file: .python-version
      - name: LLVM 18 toolchain
        run: tools/setup.sh --minimal
      - name: Verify compiler and runtime fixed points
        run: tests/verify.sh bootstrap
      - name: Package verified bootstrap
        run: python3 tools/verification_bootstrap.py export build/ci-bootstrap
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9  # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: verified-bootstrap-x86_64
          path: build/ci-bootstrap/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7
          overwrite: true

  variant:
    needs: bootstrap
    name: variant ${{ matrix.variant }} (shard ${{ matrix.shard }}, JIT and AOT)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Keep the slow optimizer rows separate; pair opt-1 with the cheaper -O0 runtime.
    # Every row still covers one quarter of the corpus in both JIT and AOT.
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        variant: [opt-1 cflags-O0, opt-2, opt-3, opt-4, opt-5, opt-6]
        shard: [0/4, 1/4, 2/4, 3/4]
    env:
      PYSTACHY_LLVM: /usr/lib/llvm-18/bin
      PYSTACHY_JOBS: '4'
      PYSTACHY_HOME: ${{ github.workspace }}
      COMPILER: ${{ github.workspace }}/build/verify/pystachy2
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false   # the tests run arbitrary programs: no token for them to read

      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0  # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version-file: .python-version

      - name: LLVM 18 toolchain
        run: tools/setup.sh --minimal

      # No run-id or token: only a producer in this workflow run can supply the compiler.
      - name: Download verified bootstrap
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333  # v8
        with:
          name: verified-bootstrap-x86_64
          path: build/ci-bootstrap
      - name: Validate and restore the native compiler
        run: python3 tools/verification_bootstrap.py restore build/ci-bootstrap

      - name: tools/variants.sh (make variants)
        id: verify-variants
        env:
          PY: python3
          VARIANTS: ${{ matrix.variant }}
          VARIANTS_SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
        run: tools/variants.sh

      - name: Record this worker's source and CPU
        if: always()
        env:
          VARIANTS: ${{ matrix.variant }}
          VARIANTS_SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
          VARIANTS_OUTCOME: ${{ steps.verify-variants.outcome }}
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import json
          import os
          import platform
          from pathlib import Path
          import subprocess
          def output(*args):
              return subprocess.check_output(args, text=True).strip()
          llvm = output(str(Path(os.environ['PYSTACHY_LLVM']) / 'opt'), '--version')
          cpu = next((line.split(':', 1)[1].strip() for line in llvm.splitlines()
                      if line.strip().startswith('Host CPU:')), 'unknown')
          report = {
              'profile': 'full', 'variants': os.environ['VARIANTS'].split(),
              'shard': os.environ['VARIANTS_SHARD'], 'modes': ['jit', 'aot'],
              'outcome': os.environ['VARIANTS_OUTCOME'],
              'git': {'commit': output('git', 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'),
                      'dirty': bool(output('git', 'status', '--porcelain'))},
              'platform': {'system': platform.platform(), 'machine': platform.machine(), 'cpu': cpu},
              'toolchain': {'python': platform.python_version(), 'llvm': llvm.splitlines()[0]},
              'run_id': os.environ['GITHUB_RUN_ID'], 'run_attempt': os.environ['GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT'],
          }
          path = Path('build/variants/worker.json')
          path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
          path.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + '\n')
          print(path.read_text(), end='')
          PY

      - name: Upload the log
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9  # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: variant-${{ matrix.variant }}-${{ strategy.job-index }}
          path: build/variants
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 14

#!/bin/sh
# The corpus (tests/run.sh, JIT and AOT) in configurations that make verify does not test and that
# must change no result (make variants; docs/testing.md#configuration-variants):
#   opt-1 ... opt-6  PYSTACHY_OPT turning off the passes on the IR (specs.py's OPTS) that rows 1 to 6
#                    of a covering array leave off. Its row 0 is every pass on, the default that verify
#                    tests (verify also turns them all off); with it, these rows run every two passes in
#                    each of their four on/off combinations. A pass's column is a distinct set of 3 of
#                    the 7 rows that includes row 0: two columns share row 0, each has a row the other
#                    lacks, and some row is in neither. Fifteen such sets exist; a new pass takes the next
#   cflags-O0        PYSTACHY_CFLAGS=-O0: the runtime unoptimized, and with it an AOT program's whole
#                    module, whose IR then runs as the compiler emitted it. The runtime's frames keep
#                    every local in memory, which changes the dead words that the conservative
#                    collector scans as roots (tools/runtime_coverage.sh's instrumented runtime is
#                    another such variant, the one whose registers exposed open()'s retention). Its
#                    JIT runs in lli (PYSTACHY_JIT_LAUNCHER=lli), the fallback of the JIT runner that
#                    every other configuration uses
# The caller's settings that the steps set, or that would change the tests, are dropped, as
# tests/verify.sh drops them; each variant builds a runtime of its own, in a temporary cache. The
# logs go to build/variants/ (so a checkout runs one at a time). Fails when a variant fails a test.
# usage: tools/variants.sh [FILE...]   (as tests/run.sh takes them; default: every case)
#   env: COMPILER (default ./pystachy), MODES (default "jit aot"), VARIANTS (default: all, in the
#        order above), VARIANTS_SHARD=I/N (shard I of N of the corpus alone, as
#        tests/verify.sh shards it: tools/shard_cases.sh), PY (default python3, to read OPTS)
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
ROOT=$(pwd)
PYS=${COMPILER:-./pystachy}
PY=${PY:-python3}
MODES=${MODES:-jit aot}
case $PYS in *" "*) ;; *) [ -x "$PYS" ] || { echo "tools/variants.sh: no compiler $PYS (make, or COMPILER=...)" >&2; exit 2; } ;; esac
ign=$(env | sed -nE 's/^(PYSTACHY_(PATH|CFLAGS|GC|GC_STRESS|GC_STRESS_PROGRAM|IRCHECK|IRFX|OPT|JIT_INLINE|JIT_CODEGEN|JIT_LAUNCHER|UNICODE_AUDIT|ARGV0))=.*$/\1/p' | sort -u)
for e in $ign; do echo "tools/variants.sh: ignoring $e=$(printenv "$e")"; unset "$e"; done
export PYSTACHY_HOME="$ROOT"
W=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pystachy-variants.XXXXXX") || exit 1
trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT TERM
L=$ROOT/build/variants
# opt-N and the PYSTACHY_OPT of row N, one a line
$PY -I - "$ROOT" > "$W/rows" <<'EOF' || { echo "tools/variants.sh: $PY cannot read OPTS (src/pystachy_compiler/specs.py)" >&2; exit 2; }
import itertools, sys
sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
from src.pystachy_compiler.specs import OPTS
cols = [c for c in itertools.combinations(range(7), 3) if 0 in c]
if len(OPTS) > len(cols):
    raise SystemExit(f"{len(OPTS)} passes, but the array has {len(cols)} columns: widen it")
rows = [[r in cols[j] for j in range(len(OPTS))] for r in range(7)]
for a, b in itertools.combinations(range(len(OPTS)), 2):
    assert len({(row[a], row[b]) for row in rows}) == 4, (OPTS[a], OPTS[b])
for r in range(1, 7):
    print(f"opt-{r}", ",".join("-" + OPTS[j] for j in range(len(OPTS)) if not rows[r][j]))
EOF
all="$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$W/rows" | tr '\n' ' ')cflags-O0"
for v in ${VARIANTS:-$all}; do
  case " $all " in *" $v "*) ;; *) echo "tools/variants.sh: no variant $v (the variants: $all)" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
done
if [ -n "${VARIANTS_SHARD:-}" ]; then
  [ $# = 0 ] || { echo "tools/variants.sh: FILEs or VARIANTS_SHARD, not both" >&2; exit 2; }
  tools/shard_cases.sh "$VARIANTS_SHARD" > "$W/cases" || exit 2
  while IFS= read -r f; do set -- "$@" "$f"; done < "$W/cases"
  [ $# != 0 ] || { echo "tools/variants.sh: shard $VARIANTS_SHARD has no case" >&2; exit 1; }
fi
rm -rf "$L"; mkdir -p "$L" || exit 1
failed=
for v in ${VARIANTS:-$all}; do
  case $v in
    opt-*) set=PYSTACHY_OPT=$(sed -n "s/^$v //p" "$W/rows") ;;
    cflags-O0) set="PYSTACHY_CFLAGS=-O0 PYSTACHY_JIT_LAUNCHER=lli" ;;
  esac
  t0=$(date +%s)
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086 # (one or two settings, VAR=VALUE each, which hold no space)
  env $set PYSTACHY_CACHE="$W/cache-$v" tests/run.sh "$PYS" "$MODES" "$@" > "$L/$v.log" 2>&1
  st=$?
  echo "$v ($set; $MODES${VARIANTS_SHARD:+; shard $VARIANTS_SHARD}): $(tail -1 "$L/$v.log") in $(($(date +%s) - t0)) s"
  grep -v '^selected ' "$L/$v.log" | sed '$d' | head -40
  case $st in
    0) ;;
    1) failed="$failed $v" ;;
    *) echo "tools/variants.sh: tests/run.sh exited with status $st" >&2; exit "$st" ;;
  esac
done
[ -z "$failed" ] || { echo "tools/variants.sh: failed:$failed (logs in build/variants/)" >&2; exit 1; }

#!/bin/sh
# The corpus cases of shard I of N, one a line, heaviest first: tests/corpus.sh's corpus_shard, as
# tests/verify.sh's shard_cases selects them, so that on every runner the N shards are disjoint and
# together are the whole corpus (rejection and syntax checks included), balanced by the weights of
# tests/case_weights.txt. tools/coverage.sh, tools/runtime_coverage.sh and tools/variants.sh run their
# shards' cases (COVERAGE_SHARD and the like).
# usage: tools/shard_cases.sh I/N   (fails with status 2 unless 0 <= I < N)
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
. tests/corpus.sh
case ${1:-} in
  [0-9]*/[0-9]*) i=${1%/*}; n=${1#*/} ;;
  *) i=x; n= ;;
esac
case $i$n in *[!0-9]*) echo "tools/shard_cases.sh: '${1:-}' is not I/N" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac
[ "$n" -gt 0 ] && [ "$i" -lt "$n" ] || { echo "tools/shard_cases.sh: no shard $i of $n" >&2; exit 2; }
corpus_shard "$i" "$n"

#!/bin/sh
# Differential tests (the corpus's layout: tests/corpus.sh). Every program tests/programs/AREA/NAME.py
# must print exactly what CPython printed (stdout + exit code, recorded in NAME.out beside it) both
# JIT-run and AOT-compiled; where CPython wrote to stderr, the last line (NAME.err) must match too,
# and where it wrote none (no NAME.err), the program must write none either; an AOT build writes
# none. Stdin comes from NAME.in; where NAME.full exists, stdout is /dev/full (writing it fails);
# where NAME.path exists, it is PYSTACHY_PATH (as PYTHONPATH was for tests/record.sh). A program
# named *_closed_stdin, *_closed_stdout or *_closed_stderr starts with that descriptor closed, for
# which CPython's sys.stdin, sys.stdout or sys.stderr is None.
# A test program dies by no signal but SIGTERM and SIGINT: bash as sh reports a death by another
# one with the process ID (and "core dumped" or not, by ulimit -c: 0 here, so that no core file
# lands in the tree). Every case runs on an 8 MiB stack (ulimit -s 8192, CI's and the usual size),
# which decides where deep recursion meets the native stack's floor
# (tests/deviations/recursion_native_stack.py), whatever the caller's.
# PYSTACHY_GC_STRESS_PROGRAM=N makes the programs collect every N allocations (JIT and AOT), whatever
# PYSTACHY_GC_STRESS gives the compiler that builds them.
# Every tests/errors/AREA/*.py must be rejected with the message in its first line (rtmode_*.py as
# "pystachy rt" compiles runtime.py; its NAME.path, if any, is PYSTACHY_PATH): exit status 1, and
# one line on stderr, the diagnostic FILE:LINE: error: MESSAGE, which holds the expected message;
# and every tests/deviations/*.py must print its hand-written .out (documented deviations from
# CPython). "pystachy check", which only parses, must accept the programs syntax_*.py and report
# the error of a rejection syntax_*.py whose error is in its own file.
# Without FILEs, it runs every case, and fails first if a test lies where none is looked for (a
# program or rejection directly in tests/, from before the corpus's areas: corpus_strays).
# The compiler checks the IR it builds (PYSTACHY_IRCHECK=1, unless set otherwise).
# The cases run in PYSTACHY_JOBS workers at once (default: one per CPU), each taking the next case
# no other worker has claimed (mkdir is atomic); the report lists them in the same order whatever
# the number of workers. Worker 0 runs in this shell and is the only one to take the cases about
# SIGINT: the other workers are asynchronous jobs, which start with SIGINT ignored.
# PYSTACHY_CASE_TIMES=FILE appends a line "MILLISECONDS CASE" for each case, in the report's order: the
# wall-clock time its worker took (needs GNU date's %N; tools/case_weights.py turns such files into the
# weights that balance tests/corpus.sh's shards).
# usage: tests/run.sh [COMPILER [MODES [FILE...]]]   (default: ./pystachy "jit aot" and every case;
#        e.g. "python3 pystachy.py", or tests/run.sh ./pystachy jit tests/programs/strings/str_*.py
#        tests/errors/syntax/x.py; FILEs are relative to the repository root)
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
. tests/corpus.sh
# shellcheck disable=SC3045 # (ulimit -c is not POSIX, but dash, bash, ksh and busybox have it)
ulimit -c 0 2> /dev/null
# shellcheck disable=SC3045 # (and -s)
ulimit -s 8192 2> /dev/null
PYS=${1:-./pystachy}
MODES=${2:-jit aot}
if [ $# -gt 2 ]; then shift 2; else set --; fi
nsel=$#; seen=" "
for f; do
  f=${f#./}
  case $f in tests/programs/*/*.py | tests/deviations/*.py | tests/errors/*/*.py) [ -f "$f" ] ;; *) false ;; esac || {
    echo "tests/run.sh: not a test: $f (programs are tests/programs/AREA/*.py, rejections tests/errors/AREA/*.py)" >&2; exit 2; }
  # once each (two copies of a case would write the same files at once, from two workers)
  case $seen in *" $f "*) continue ;; esac
  seen="$seen$f "; set -- "$@" "$f"
done
shift $nsel
T=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pystachy-tests.XXXXXX") || exit 1
pids=
trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
if [ $nsel = 0 ]; then
  corpus_strays > "$T/strays"
  if [ -s "$T/strays" ]; then
    echo "tests/run.sh: no run tests these files, which lie outside the corpus's areas (tests/corpus.sh):" >&2
    cat "$T/strays" >&2; exit 2
  fi
  corpus > "$T/corpus"
  while IFS= read -r f; do set -- "$@" "$f"; done < "$T/corpus"
fi
[ $# != 0 ] || { echo "tests/run.sh: no test cases" >&2; exit 2; }
export PYSTACHY_IRCHECK="${PYSTACHY_IRCHECK:-1}"
JOBS=${PYSTACHY_JOBS:-$( (nproc || getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN) 2> /dev/null)}
case $JOBS in '' | *[!0-9]* | 0) JOBS=1 ;; esac
XENV=${PYSTACHY_GC_STRESS_PROGRAM:+env PYSTACHY_GC_STRESS=$PYSTACHY_GC_STRESS_PROGRAM}  # (an AOT program's)
TIMES=${PYSTACHY_CASE_TIMES:-}
if [ -n "$TIMES" ]; then
  case $(date +%s%N) in
    '' | *[!0-9]*) echo "tests/run.sh: no case times (PYSTACHY_CASE_TIMES needs date +%s%N, GNU date's)" >&2; TIMES= ;;
  esac
fi
# Ctrl-C or TERM: name the cases that were running (on fd 4, this script's stdout), stop the workers
trap 'for f in "$T"/now.*; do [ -f "$f" ] && echo "INTERRUPTED while running $(cat "$f")" >&4; done; kill $pids 2> /dev/null; exit 130' INT TERM
exec 3> /dev/full 4>&1
# the cases about SIGINT, found once (one grep, not one per case and worker)
SIG=" $(grep -lE 'kill -INT|KeyboardInterrupt' "$@" | while read -r f; do printf '%s ' "$f"; done)"

# Each case adds to $pass and $fail and prints what the report shows for it.
program() { # tests/programs/AREA/NAME.py, its sidecars B.in, B.out... (B: the path without .py)
  b=${1%.py}; n=${b##*/}; in=/dev/null; [ -f "$b.in" ] && in="$b.in"
  o=1; [ -f "$b.full" ] && o=3
  si=0 se=2                            # (<&$si >&$o 2>&$se: "-" closes that descriptor)
  case $n in *_closed_stdin) si=- ;; *_closed_stdout) o=- ;; *_closed_stderr) se=- ;; esac
  mp=$PYSTACHY_PATH
  if [ -f "$b.path" ]; then
    mp=$(sh tests/prepare_path.sh "$1" "$T") || {
      fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "FAIL $n: cannot prepare import path"; return;
    }
  fi
  for mode in $MODES; do
    # the program's stderr goes to $n.err, an AOT build's to $n.build, which must stay empty (what
    # pystachy run writes before it becomes the program goes to $n.err: it must be nothing too)
    : > "$T/$n.build"; : > "$T/$n.err"
    if [ $mode = jit ]; then
      (PYSTACHY_PATH=$mp $PYS run "$1" a1 a2 < "$in" <&$si >&$o 2>&$se; echo "[exit $?]") > "$T/$n.$mode" 2> "$T/$n.err"
    else
      PYSTACHY_PATH=$mp $PYS build "$1" -o "$T/$n.exe" 2> "$T/$n.build" &&
        ($XENV "$T/$n.exe" a1 a2 < "$in" <&$si >&$o 2>&$se; echo "[exit $?]") > "$T/$n.$mode" 2> "$T/$n.err"
    fi
    if cmp -s "$T/$n.$mode" "$b.out" && [ ! -s "$T/$n.build" ] &&
      if [ -f "$b.err" ]; then [ "$(tail -1 "$T/$n.err")" = "$(cat "$b.err")" ]; else [ ! -s "$T/$n.err" ]; fi; then
      pass=$((pass + 1)); else
      fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "FAIL $n ($mode)"; diff "$b.out" "$T/$n.$mode" | head -10
      if [ -f "$b.err" ]; then echo "  stderr: want '$(cat "$b.err")', got '$(tail -1 "$T/$n.err")'"
      elif [ -s "$T/$n.err" ]; then echo "  stderr: want none (CPython wrote none), got:"; fi
      head -5 "$T/$n.err"
      [ ! -s "$T/$n.build" ] || { echo "  build's stderr:"; head -5 "$T/$n.build"; }
    fi
  done
  case $n in
    syntax_*)
      if $PYS check "$1" > "$T/chk.$n" 2>&1 && [ ! -s "$T/chk.$n" ]; then pass=$((pass + 1)); else
        fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "FAIL $n (check)"; head -5 "$T/chk.$n"; fi ;;
  esac
}
# Documented deviations from CPython: tests/deviations/*.out is written by hand and holds
# stdout and stderr together (the runtime flushes stdout before reporting an error).
deviation() { # tests/deviations/NAME.py
  n=${1##*/}; n=${n%.py}; exp="tests/deviations/$n.out"
  for mode in $MODES; do
    if [ $mode = jit ]; then
      ($PYS run "$1" a1 a2 < /dev/null 2>&1; echo "[exit $?]") > "$T/dev.$n.$mode"
    else
      { $PYS build "$1" -o "$T/dev.$n.exe" 2>&1 && $XENV "$T/dev.$n.exe" a1 a2 < /dev/null 2>&1; echo "[exit $?]"; } > "$T/dev.$n.$mode"
    fi
    if cmp -s "$T/dev.$n.$mode" "$exp"; then pass=$((pass + 1)); else
      fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "FAIL deviations/$n ($mode)"; diff "$exp" "$T/dev.$n.$mode" | head -10; fi
  done
}
# A rejection exits with status 1 and writes one line to stderr, the diagnostic FILE:LINE: error:
# MESSAGE, which holds the expected message (diag ERRFILE: that is what ERRFILE holds, and nothing
# after that line's newline: the second read finds no data, not even text without a newline)
diag() {
  { IFS= read -r line && ! IFS= read -r more && [ -z "$more" ]; } < "$1" || return 1
  case $line in *.py:[0-9]*": error: "*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
  case $line in *"$want"*) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
}
rejection() { # tests/errors/AREA/NAME.py
  n=${1##*/}; n=${n%.py}
  IFS= read -r want < "$1"
  want=${want#"# error: "}
  how=ir
  case $n in rtmode_*) how=rt ;; esac  # compiled as runtime.py is
  mp=$PYSTACHY_PATH
  if [ -f "${1%.py}.path" ]; then
    mp=$(sh tests/prepare_path.sh "$1" "$T") || {
      fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "FAIL $n: cannot prepare import path"; return;
    }
  fi
  PYSTACHY_PATH=$mp $PYS $how "$1" > /dev/null 2> "$T/rej.$n"; st=$?
  if [ $st = 1 ] && diag "$T/rej.$n"; then pass=$((pass + 1)); else
    fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "FAIL $1: expected error '$want', got (exit $st): $(cat "$T/rej.$n")"; fi
  case $n:$want in
    syntax_*:"$n.py:"*)
      $PYS check "$1" > /dev/null 2> "$T/chk.$n"; st=$?
      if [ $st = 1 ] && diag "$T/chk.$n"; then pass=$((pass + 1)); else
        fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "FAIL $1 (check): expected error '$want', got (exit $st): $(cat "$T/chk.$n")"; fi ;;
  esac
}
# worker K CASE...: each case no worker has claimed yet (claiming creates $T/c.I), the cases about
# SIGINT only if K is 0; case I's report goes to $T/I.log and its counts to $T/I.n
worker() {
  k=$1; shift; i=0
  for t; do
    if [ ! -d "$T/c.$i" ]; then
      case $SIG in *" $t "*) [ "$k" = 0 ] ;; *) true ;; esac && mkdir "$T/c.$i" 2> /dev/null && {
        pass=0; fail=0; echo "$t" > "$T/now.$k"
        [ -z "$TIMES" ] || t0=$(date +%s%N)
        {
          case $t in
            tests/deviations/*) deviation "$t" ;;
            tests/errors/*/*) rejection "$t" ;;
            *) program "$t" ;;
          esac
        } > "$T/$i.log" 2>&1
        [ -z "$TIMES" ] || echo $((($(date +%s%N) - t0) / 1000000)) > "$T/$i.ms"
        echo "$pass $fail" > "$T/$i.n"
      }
    fi
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  rm -f "$T/now.$k"
}
# the cached runtime is built once, before the workers start (each would rebuild a stale one)
echo pass > "$T/warm.py" || exit 1
if $PYS run "$T/warm.py" > "$T/warm.log" 2>&1; then :; else
  st=$?
  echo "tests/run.sh: runtime cache preparation failed (exit $st)" >&2
  cat "$T/warm.log" >&2
  exit 1
fi
k=1
while [ $k -lt "$JOBS" ]; do
  worker $k "$@" &
  pids="$pids $!"; k=$((k + 1))
done
worker 0 "$@"
wait
pass=0; fail=0; i=0
for t; do
  if [ -f "$T/$i.n" ]; then
    # Successful cases normally have empty logs; keep missing-file diagnostics and failure output.
    if [ ! -f "$T/$i.log" ] || [ -s "$T/$i.log" ]; then cat "$T/$i.log"; fi
    read -r p f < "$T/$i.n"
    pass=$((pass + p)); fail=$((fail + f))
    if [ -n "$TIMES" ] && [ -f "$T/$i.ms" ] && read -r ms < "$T/$i.ms"; then printf '%s %s\n' "$ms" "$t" >> "$TIMES"; fi
  else
    fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "FAIL $t: no result (its worker died)"
  fi
  i=$((i + 1))
done
[ $nsel = 0 ] || echo "selected $# cases"
echo "$pass passed, $fail failed"
[ $fail = 0 ]
